title: Our 10 favorite scenes from T2: Judgment Day
gist: A retrospective and rerelease-tie-in listicle on Terminator 2: Judgment Day's 35th anniversary, covering its production history, visual-effects innovations, and box-office performance, with essentially no market or technology-investment signal beyond film-industry trivia.

insights.claim: The original 1984 Terminator cost about $6.4 million to make and grossed roughly $78 million, prompting Arnold Schwarzenegger to push for a sequel.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Illustrates a historical example of outsized sequel-driven ROI in the film industry, though it has no bearing on current markets.
insights.locator: Nobody really expected 1984’s The Terminator to be a hit

insights.claim: Terminator 2: Judgment Day had an estimated production budget of about $70 million and went on to gross $520 million worldwide, despite predictions it would bomb.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A high-risk, high-budget effects tentpole paying off at roughly 7x its budget despite pre-release skepticism — a data point on blockbuster economics, though decades old and not actionable today.
insights.locator: Released over the July 4th holiday weekend in 1991

insights.claim: Despite T2's massive box-office success, its production studio Carolco Pictures still went bankrupt in 1995 due to losses on other films.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A cautionary historical example that even a single blockbuster hit doesn't guarantee studio survival if the broader portfolio underperforms — a durable lesson about single-hit dependency risk in content-production businesses.
insights.locator: which sadly was not enough to protect Carolco

insights.claim: Industrial Light & Magic made a major investment — expanding staff and spending over $3 million on new equipment and specially designed software — to create the shapeshifting T-1000 character's liquid-metal effects for T2.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: An early example of a VFX studio making a large capital bet on new CGI capability ahead of proven demand, which paid off critically and commercially and is credited with helping usher in the modern CGI era.
insights.locator: ILM made a major investment, expanding its staff

insights.claim: StudioCanal is staging a staggered international theatrical rerelease of T2 for its 35th anniversary, rolling out country by country from late August through early September across Germany, the US, France, the UK, and others.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Reflects the ongoing studio practice of monetizing legacy IP through anniversary theatrical rereleases rather than relying solely on streaming/home video revenue.
insights.locator: There is a staggered global rollout for the rerelease
